text: Here are my notes from the incident review. The outage began at 02:14 when the primary load balancer health check started failing. Traffic failed over to the secondary but the secondary had a stale TLS certificate, so roughly 40% of requests returned handshake errors for eleven minutes. The on-call engineer was paged at 02:17 and acknowledged at 02:21. Root cause was that certificate renewal automation had been disabled during a migration three weeks earlier and nobody noticed because the alert for it routed to a deprecated channel. We restored service by manually installing the renewed certificate at 02:33. Follow-ups discussed: re-enable renewal automation, add a synthetic check for certificate expiry, and audit every alert route for dead channels. Please turn all of that into a formal postmortem with a timeline table and a numbered action item list.
